idiom_name: tower::retry / reqwest-retry middleware + a uuid key in the request
implementation_notes: The replay half is tower middleware: RetryLayer with a Policy, or reqwest-retry's RetryTransientMiddleware bound to an ExponentialBackoff RetryPolicy inside a reqwest_middleware ClientBuilder, so no hand-written loop is needed. Middleware re-executes the whole request future, which is why the key must already be part of the request description: generate uuid::Uuid::new_v4() once per logical operation and attach it as a header before the client runs, never inside the future the layer retries. The type system helps with the other half: Result makes failure explicit at the API boundary, and a request body that cannot be replayed (a stream) simply cannot be retried through the layer.
pitfalls: The retry layer replays the request future, so a key computed inside the async block or in a per-attempt closure is a fresh UUID for every attempt.
Retry layers need a clonable, replayable body; streaming bodies fail or replay partially, so keyed retries should carry a buffered body.

reqwest surfaces timeouts and connection resets as Err after the request may have been processed - model an explicit 'unknown outcome' instead of collapsing it into a generic error the caller will retry blindly.
